findings.text: non-blocking: the head arm of the negative control the manifest names was run at 0e7703803a95b0df314aa2b29632b1c20829c9a4, a commit on top of the reviewed head whose diff against 37cd777f16 rewrites reckon/ledger.py and adds 68 lines to reckon/file_memo.py, so the control's green side is not the revision this record names; the red side (2 failed, 1 passed, EXIT=1 on the reverted tree) still shows the checks fire, and after_suite-1795084301682773877.log independently reports 64 passed EXIT=0 at 37cd777f16.

non-blocking: _handed_rows copies each row dict but shares every nested value, and _PICKER_FIELDS at reckon/ledger.py:1700-1726 includes the nested budget, throughput and lane_receipt, so a caller that patches a nested field changes what the next reader of the held history is handed, which ledger.load's per-read json.loads never allowed; the guard at tests/test_budget_and_picker_history_read_what_changed.py:348 patches only a top-level key and pops a row, so it cannot catch this.

non-blocking: test_concurrent_reads_keep_their_own_history is not a guard for _HELD_LOCK at reckon/ledger.py:1766 — the run's own revert log records the arm as 'F.F', i.e. this test passed (1 passed) against the pre-repair container that holds no lock, so removing the lock again would leave it green; it asserts only the content of each answer and names no condition under which a lost or half-replaced entry makes it fail.

item_verdicts.manifest: read at the reviewed head; it records commits ad7a0a8775, 4d3102ae46, 08cf09dc1d and 37cd777f16, the scoped gate as 64 passed EXIT=0 at 37cd777f16 on all_debug, matched arms as base 58 passed and head 64 passed, both EXIT=0, and three negative-control logs.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the node declared reckon/budget.py, reckon/ledger.py, tests/test_budget_and_picker_history_read_what_changed.py and two docs paths; the gained commit touches only reckon/ledger.py and the node test, both declared.

justifications.durability: tests/test_budget_and_picker_history_read_what_changed.py:268 and :348 fail on the pre-repair container (negative-control-revert-answering-commit.log records 2 failed, 1 passed, EXIT=1), but :309 passes against that same unlocked tree and the nested-value case the ledger.py:1849 docstring promises is untested.
justifications.evidence: the gate log scoped-gate-1795084181568961223.log was run at 37cd777f1695 and records "64 passed" with EXIT=0, and the matched arm after_suite-1795084301682773877.log records "64 passed" with EXIT=0 against baseline_suite-1795084258346863040.log's "58 passed" EXIT=0, but the cited negative control's head arm was run at 0e7703803a, not the reviewed head.
justifications.fit: reckon/ledger.py:1770-1778 replaces the hand-rolled eviction loop with functools.lru_cache over a cell and keeps the module's comment-and-docstring idiom, adding only the private names _Entry, _HELD_LOCK, _history_cell, _held_history and _handed_rows.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/ledger.py:1892-1894 and :1927 hand every reader its own row dicts and :1786-1795 keep the held entry behind one lock, so the readers still answer only what was promoted since while the two defects the earlier review named are removed by the same commit.
justifications.reuse: reckon/ledger.py:1770 now leaves the bound, eviction and clear to functools.lru_cache rather than implementing them, but the repository's owner of a bounded memo, reckon/file_memo.py:445 memoized_key, is still not extended or reused, so a second bounded container over the same rows remains at reckon/ledger.py:1759-1795.
justifications.scope_discipline: the gained commit touches only reckon/ledger.py and tests/test_budget_and_picker_history_read_what_changed.py, both inside the node's declared write paths.
